source.title: Exploring the coherence of features explanations in the GemmaScope

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a GemmaScope SAE to examine feature explanations, but does not test whether superposition occurs, its geometry, or the capacity account.
record.gate_note: The study discusses superposition and polysemanticity, but its reported results concern the coherence of SAE feature explanations for animal-word inputs. Table 1 reports explanation-category counts by activation rank; these do not measure the claim versions directly.
record.test_reason: The study runs Gemma-2b inputs through a GemmaScope SAE and scores how well the pre-generated LLM explanations of the top-5 features match animal words. That measures explanation quality under a regex heuristic, not superposition geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes, dictionary recovery, feature canonicality or dimensionality. The authors themselves name the heuristic, model size, SAE size and location as possible causes, so the low coherence cannot be read as evidence about any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that top-5 feature explanations at the layer-25 post-MLP residual SAE are largely incoherent with the animal inputs, and they stress the exploratory nature of the work. They also attribute the result possibly to their shallow heuristic, the small model, the SAE's size and sparsity (residual polysemanticity), or the single layer choice. They add that showcased Neuronpedia examples may be cherry-picked.
record.recipe_differences: No original superposition method is reproduced. The study applies a GemmaScope SAE and a heuristic explanation-coherence assessment.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares explanation categories across activation ranks top1 through top5; it reports that top2 has the most category-1 explanations (29), versus 12 at top1. Only one model and SAE location are examined.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 111 single-token animal words, most GemmaScope 16K layer-25 residual SAE top-1 to top-5 feature explanations were judged incoherent by a regex heuristic. Top-2 had more animal-related explanations (29) than top-1 (12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automatic LLM explanations of highly activating SAE features often fail to match the input concept, at least for Gemma-2b layer 25 with this SAE and this heuristic.

record.problems: The analysis covers 111 animal words, one model, and one SAE location. Its explanation-coherence assessment uses simple regular expressions and pattern matching; the authors note that coherent explanations using synonyms or related terms may be missed. No controls or uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: No toy models; no test of near-orthogonal overlapping directions, the sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity.
Mentions training noise as an alternative cause only in passing; no test.
Uses SAE features but does not test whether features are distributed across neurons or whether the SAE recovers true sparse features.
Assesses the coherence of LLM explanations, not the completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a BlueDot course project on LessWrong. There are no controls, no uncertainty estimates and no human validation of the heuristic. The authors' speculation that the SAE may not fully resolve superposition is not tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test overlapping near-orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Mentions noise during training as a possible alternative explanation, but does not test polysemanticity or that alternative.
Uses SAE features from Gemma-2b, but does not test feature spreading across neurons or whether a dictionary recovers sparse features.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units; it assesses the relevance of their automatic explanations.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions.

rows.subject: Gemma-2b
rows.operation_detail: Counted explanation categories for the top-1 activating SAE feature for each target word using the stated heuristic.
rows.measure: Count of explanations in heuristic categories 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, respectively
rows.note: Aggregate counts across 111 target words. Category 0 is no coherent explanation; categories 1–4 are the specified animal, hypernym, target-concept, and word-mention categories. The flattened table is assigned by rank and category order; the counts sum to 111.
rows.check: Values are read correctly from Table 1 (98,12,0,1,0). The note mislabels category 1: per the text it is explanations about animals in general, not the specific animal. Category 3 is the specific target concept.
